properties.summary: Designs and builds cathodoluminescence tools that inspect wafers for defects, including GaN wafers. Attolight is an EPFL spin-off with about 30 staff.

properties.company: Carl Zeiss SMT (Carl Zeiss SMT Switzerland AG)
properties.products: Special actuators and complex mechatronic assemblies used in semiconductor lithography (wafer exposure) systems, not complete scanners. Site was formerly Beyond Gravity's Lithography Division, acquired by ZEISS SMT in 2024. Broader ZEISS SMT portfolio covers DUV/EUV/High-NA-EUV lithography optics and metrology, but Zurich's specific product scope in public sources is limited to precision actuators/mechatronics.
properties.sole_source_note: No public evidence that this specific site is a sole global source; parent ZEISS SMT is sole source for EUV lithography optics at the group level, but Zurich's own product scope (actuators/mechatronics) is not documented as unique to Earth.
properties.employees_basis: Combined headcount across Zurich + Coswig sites at time of acquisition ("more than 200 employees" per Beyond Gravity press release, 2024) — not a Zurich-only figure.
properties.summary: Makes special actuators and mechatronic assemblies for lithography systems in Zurich, Switzerland. Carl Zeiss SMT acquired the site from Beyond Gravity in 2024.

employees.note: Zeiss gives about 220 employees for Coswig and Zurich together (Beyond Gravity lithography division, closed 1 Dec 2024); no per-site figure was found.

properties.company: Comet Group (Comet AG / Comet Holding AG)
properties.products: RF power generators for plasma processes in chip making, and X-ray modules for industrial testing. Comet does not split the Flamatt site by division.
properties.sole_source_note: No defensible sole-source claim found; Comet is a significant but not sole supplier of RF power generators/X-ray inspection modules — competitors exist (e.g., MKS Instruments/ENI, Advanced Energy in RF power).
properties.employees_basis: Only group-wide (global) headcount is publicly disclosed by Comet Group/ZoomInfo; no site-level Flamatt headcount figure is publicly reported, so employees field is omitted.
properties.summary: Head office of Comet Group, which makes RF power generators for plasma processing and X-ray modules for industrial inspection. The split by product at this site is not public.

properties.site_name: Evatec AG Headquarters & Manufacturing Plant, Trübbach
properties.products: PVD (physical vapor deposition) thin-film process systems — sputtering and evaporation equipment — plus retrofit modules and spare parts, serving power semiconductor, RF, MEMS, and advanced packaging markets.
properties.sole_source_note: Evatec is one of several PVD equipment makers globally (competitors include Applied Materials, Oerlikon successors, ULVAC); no defensible sole-source claim.
properties.employees_basis: No site-level headcount disclosed; only company-wide estimates exist (LinkedIn: 501-1000 globally; ZoomInfo: 715 globally). Not stated how many are at Trübbach specifically.
properties.summary: Evatec in Trübbach, Switzerland, builds PVD (physical vapor deposition) sputtering and evaporation tools. They are used for power chips, RF chips, MEMS and advanced packaging.

properties.products: NanoFrazor thermal scanning probe lithography (t-SPL) systems for nanopatterning, R&D and mask-level direct-write lithography; site does instrument/materials development and application support
properties.sole_source_note: NanoFrazor is a niche/leading t-SPL tool but not established here as the only source on Earth for any specific chip-production-critical capability; insufficient evidence to claim sole-source status.
properties.employees_basis: LinkedIn company page lists 11-50 employees for Heidelberg Instruments Nano (Zurich entity); midpoint used as rough estimate, not an official disclosed figure
properties.summary: Heidelberg Instruments Nano, formerly SwissLitho, develops NanoFrazor systems in Zurich. They pattern nanostructures with a heated scanning probe. About 30 staff work at the site.

properties.site_name: VAT Vakuumventile AG — Global HQ, Manufacturing & R&D
properties.products: High-performance vacuum valves (gate, angle, pendulum, multi-valve modules), metal bellows and related high-vacuum components used primarily in semiconductor manufacturing equipment (also display, photovoltaic, and vacuum-coating equipment applications). VAT holds roughly 75% global market share in vacuum valves for semiconductor production.
properties.sole_source_note: Not sole source in the strict "only maker on Earth" sense — other vacuum valve makers exist (e.g. Presys, MKS/VAT competitors). However VAT is dominant with ~75% global market share in semiconductor vacuum valves, making it a critical near-monopoly chokepoint, but not literally the sole global source.
properties.employees_basis: Site-level headcount not publicly disclosed. Only group-wide figures are available (approx. 3,200 employees worldwide across manufacturing sites in Switzerland/Haag, Malaysia, and Romania, per VAT corporate/LinkedIn info; an older Kompass entry cites ~1,200, likely outdated or scope-limited). No source breaks out Haag-specific employee count.
properties.summary: Headquarters and factory for vacuum valves used mainly in chip equipment. VAT says it holds about 75% of the global market for these valves.

properties.products: Plasma etch and deposition systems for semiconductor and compound-materials processing: ICP and RIE etch tools, PECVD, ICP-CVD, sputtering, and thermal/plasma ALD systems.
properties.sole_source_note: Not a sole source — multiple competitors (e.g. Oxford Instruments' own peers such as SPTS/KLA, Plasma-Therm, SAMCO) make comparable plasma etch/deposition equipment.
properties.employees_basis: No site-specific headcount publicly disclosed; only company-wide Oxford Instruments plc figures exist, which are not attributable to this site alone.
properties.summary: Headquarters and factory for plasma etch and deposition tools, including ICP etch, PECVD, sputtering and ALD (atomic layer deposition) systems.

properties.site_name: Plasma-Therm UK Ltd (Specialty Process Engineering Group)
properties.products: Custom plasma process equipment and engineering, complementary to Plasma-Therm's etch, deposition and advanced packaging tools. Plasma-Therm names no product line for this site.
properties.sole_source_note: No defensible sole-source claim; site's specific output is not publicly itemized, and Plasma-Therm has multiple global sites (US, France/CORIAL).
properties.employees_basis: Not disclosed at site level; only US HQ (St. Petersburg, FL) headcount of ~91 is publicly reported, which does not apply to this UK site
properties.summary: Engineering site in Somerton, UK, for custom plasma process equipment for etch and deposition. It joined Plasma-Therm through a 2020 acquisition.

properties.site_name: KLA SPTS Division R&D and Manufacturing Facility
properties.products: Advanced etch and deposition wafer-processing equipment (plasma etch, PVD, CVD, MVD, PECVD tool platforms) for advanced packaging, MEMS, RF, power devices, photonics, LEDs, and sensors. Site includes 25,000 sq ft of R&D clean rooms and 35,000 sq ft of manufacturing space within a 237,000 sq ft facility.
properties.sole_source_note: SPTS/KLA is a major supplier of MEMS/advanced-packaging etch and deposition tools but not the sole global source for these equipment categories (competitors include Oxford Instruments Plasma Technology, AMAT, Tokyo Electron, ASM International).
properties.employees_basis: KLA's own press release/location-spotlight page states ~500 employees based in Newport, with the new facility built to a capacity of 750; no independently verified third-party site headcount figure found.
properties.summary: Builds plasma etch and deposition tools for packaging, MEMS, RF and power chips. KLA opened a new $138M Newport facility in May 2025, with 500 employees.

properties.products: Etch and deposition process equipment for semiconductor/MEMS manufacturing (proprietary tools Solo, Sentry, Multi - dry release etch and deposition), plus new and remanufactured/refurbished front-end etch and deposition systems and related process services.
properties.sole_source_note: No defensible sole-source claim found; memsstar is one of several MEMS/semiconductor etch-and-deposition equipment suppliers.
properties.employees_basis: Company-wide headcount (not confirmed site-only) from Companies House-linked filings/analytics (Pomanda ~29, PitchBook 29, Endole 28, ZoomInfo 26, LinkedIn 11-50 band). This is the company's only known facility, so likely approximates site headcount, but not explicitly stated as site-level.
properties.summary: memsstar in Livingston, Scotland, makes etch and deposition tools for chips and MEMS. It also sells refurbished etch and deposition systems. The company has about 29 employees.

properties.products: Advanced optical overlay and film metrology equipment, including key sub-assemblies, used for process control in chip manufacturing.
properties.sole_source_note: KLA is a major metrology supplier but other firms (e.g. Onto Innovation, Nova, ASML's HMI) sell overlay and film metrology tools; no sole-source claim.
properties.employees_basis: Figures of about 268 to 270 appear in an employer profile and a regional business profile; neither was opened, so not recorded.
properties.summary: KLA-Tencor MIE in Weilburg makes optical overlay and film metrology equipment for chip process control. The European Commission approved a €74.4m German grant in July 2026.

properties.products: MOCVD (metal-organic chemical vapor deposition) systems for compound semiconductor production.
properties.sole_source_note: Aixtron is the largest MOCVD supplier (company cites a 77% 2024 share, Yole estimate) but Veeco and others also sell MOCVD tools; no sole-source claim.
properties.employees_basis: No site-level headcount published; group figure 1,117 at Dec 2025.
properties.summary: Makes MOCVD (metal organic vapor deposition) systems for compound semiconductors, with R&D, in Cambridge. Aixtron cites a 77% MOCVD market share for 2024.

properties.products: MOCVD (metal-organic chemical vapor deposition) systems for compound semiconductor production.
properties.sole_source_note: Aixtron is the largest MOCVD supplier (company cites a 77% 2024 share, Yole estimate) but Veeco and others also sell MOCVD tools; no sole-source claim.
properties.employees_basis: No site-level headcount published; group figure 1,117 at Dec 2025.
properties.summary: Production of MOCVD (metal organic chemical vapor deposition) systems for compound semiconductors. Aixtron bought the site near Turin in 2024.
